prompt: Users upload photos and videos up to 4 GB each. The relational database is growing by a terabyte a week.
why: Put the files in object storage (S3, GCS) and keep only their keys and metadata in the database.
trap: Sharding the database just spreads huge blobs over more databases.

prompt: Large video uploads pass through your app servers and tie them up for minutes.
why: Hand out pre-signed URLs so clients upload straight to object storage.
trap: More app servers behind a balancer still waste them on byte shuffling.

prompt: Nightly database backups of 2 TB must be kept for seven years at low cost.
tells: kept for seven years at low cost
why: Object storage with lifecycle rules to move old backups to archival tiers.
trap: A replica is a live copy, not a 7-year history.

prompt: Data scientists share 500 GB training datasets that never change once written.
why: Large immutable files are exactly what object storage is for.
trap: Caching assumes small hot items, not half-terabyte files.

prompt: Paying customers download private PDF reports, and links must expire after an hour so they can't be shared forever.
tells: links must expire after an hour
why: Store files in object storage and hand out pre-signed URLs with a 1-hour expiry.
trap: A CDN can front it, but the expiring access comes from signed URLs on the bucket.

prompt: Log files are read often for a week, rarely for a year, then never. Storage costs keep climbing.
why: Object storage lifecycle rules move files to cheaper tiers as they age.
trap: More database shards would only spread the cost around.

prompt: A team wants to host a static documentation site of HTML, CSS and images with no servers to manage.
why: A bucket can serve static files directly (usually with a CDN in front).
trap: The CDN speeds it up; the bucket is where it lives.

prompt: Uploads of 20 GB scientific datasets over flaky connections keep failing at 90% and restarting from zero.
why: Use multipart uploads to object storage so only failed parts are retried.
trap: Retries alone don't help if each one starts over.
